hints: The complete set should contain exactly one copy of each number from 1 through n.
Compare the sum of 1..n with the sum of the n-1 provided values.
Subtract the provided sum; distinctness and range guarantees identify the missing value.
analogy: It is like totaling a complete numbered ticket roll and subtracting the tickets you still have.
example: For n=5, 1+2+3+4+5=15; given 2,3,1,5 totals 11, so 15-11=4 is missing.
algorithm: Use the arithmetic-series sum n(n+1)/2, subtract the input sum, and print the difference. Use a wide integer for the total.
correctness: The input contains every required number except one exactly once, so the difference between the full and observed sums is exactly that number.
complexity: O(n) time to read values and O(1) extra space.
